title: Technology Sector Update for 05/29/2018: ZTO,BABA,MOMO,AAPL

Technology stocks were mostly declining Tuesday, with shares of tech companies in the S&P 500 losing over 0.8% in value while the Philadelphia semiconductor index also was posting a more than 0.8% retreat.
Among technology stocks moving on news:
+ ZTO Express ( ZTO ) was nearly 8% higher Tuesday afternoon, retracing most of a more than 12% advance to a best-ever $21.70 per American depositary share that followed online retailer Alibaba ( BABA ) saying it was partnering with Cainiao to invest $1.38 billion in the Chinese delivery company. Alibaba is expecting the deal will see Cainiao and ZTO Express extend their current collaborations and also better embrace the New Retail concept developed by Alibaba promoting seamless integration between online and offline commerce. The investment also will support the focus by both Cainiao and ZTO on improving first- and final-mile pickup and delivery capabilities, warehouse management, cross-border logistics and technology-driven smart services, the companies said.
In other sector news:
+ Momo ( MOMO ) surged on Tuesday, racing as much as 13% higher, after the Chinese information technology company reported better-than-expected non-GAAP Q1 net income and revenue. Excluding one-time items, the company earned $0.69 per American depositary share, up from $0.44 per ADS during the same quarter last year and beating the Capital IQ consensus by $0.19 per ADS. Total net revenue climbed to $435.1 million from $265.2 million during the year-ago period and also topping the $398.3 million analyst mean. Looking forward to the current quarter, the company is projecting a 51% to 55% increase in Q2 revenue over year-ago levels to a range of $470.0 million to $485.0 million compared the Street view modelling $429.8 million in Q2 revenue. The company's forecast includes around $4.5 million in revenue expected from its Tantan unit during June, which it expects to add to its Q2 financial results.
- Apple ( AAPL ) was narrowly lower in recent trading, bouncing off a brief jump on positive ground for the second time on Tuesday following reports the tech giant plans to use OLED screens on at least three of its iPhone models in 2019. The new phones are expected to come out during Apple's traditional September release window, according to MacRumors, citing a report in South Korea's Electronic Times.
